issues.legal_issue: The statutory exception for income settled on another person requires both the prescribed period of non-revocability and the absence of any direct or indirect benefit to the settlor from that person's income.
material_facts: The trust provided for income to be distributed among the settlor and other beneficiaries.
The settlor's income as a beneficiary was distinct from the shares distributed to the other beneficiaries.
issues.conclusion: The exception protects only the part of the trust income arising to another person if the trust satisfies the non-revocability condition and the settlor derives no direct or indirect benefit from that person's income.
issues.legal_principle: Under the third proviso to s. 16(1)(c) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, both the required period of non-revocability and the absence of a direct or indirect benefit to the settlor from the income given to the beneficiary must be established. The proviso excludes only the qualifying income arising to another person; it does not exempt the whole trust merely because some income meets those conditions.

predicates.income_tax_assessment_proceeding: The matter concerns assessment of a settlor's income for income tax.
predicates.income_arises_to_another_beneficiary: The trust distributes income to a person other than the settlor.
predicates.trust_not_revocable_within_prescribed_pe: The trust cannot be revoked during the period required for the statutory exception.
predicates.settlor_gets_no_benefit_from_other_benef: The settlor derives no direct or indirect benefit from the income distributed to the other beneficiary.

issues.definition: When an income-tax assessment concerns income distributed to another beneficiary, the qualifying income is excluded from the settlor's taxable income if the trust cannot be revoked during the required period and the settlor gets no benefit from that income.

issues.legal_issue: A trust whose terms prevent revocation while leases remain effective beyond six years is not revocable within six years for the purposes of the statutory exception.
material_facts: The amended trust deed made the settlement irrevocable while specified leases remained effective, whichever of the relevant events occurred last.
One lease was to remain effective until 1965 and another until 1954.
issues.conclusion: The trust was not revocable within six years as provided by s. 16(1)(c).
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the trust deed with the third proviso to s. 16(1)(c) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, and relied on Ramji Keshavji v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay, 13 I.T.R. 105, in explaining the operation of the provisos to that section.

predicates.income_tax_assessment_proceeding: The matter concerns an income-tax assessment involving income arising under a trust.
predicates.deed_bars_revocation_while_lease_remains: The trust deed prevents the settlor from revoking the trust while a specified lease remains effective.
predicates.lease_continues_beyond_six_years: The specified lease remains effective for more than six years from the trust's creation.

issues.definition: In an income-tax assessment, a trust is not revocable within six years when its deed bars revocation while a lease continues beyond six years.

issues.legal_issue: Income distributed to other beneficiaries under a qualifying trust cannot be included in the settlor's income until the power to revoke arises, but the settlor's own beneficial income remains taxable.
material_facts: The settlor created a trust distributing income among herself, her husband, and her five sons.
The deed prevented revocation while specified leases remained effective beyond six years.
The settlor was herself entitled to a share of the trust income.
issues.conclusion: The income received by beneficiaries other than the settlor could not be deemed to be the settlor's income until her power to revoke arose; the settlor remained liable to tax on income received as a beneficiary.
issues.legal_principle: Under s. 16(1)(c) and its third proviso of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, qualifying income distributed to another person is excluded from the settlor's income until the power to revoke arises. The third proviso does not exclude income that the settlor receives in her own capacity as a beneficiary. The Court relied on Ramji Keshavji v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay, 13 I.T.R. 105, in explaining the statutory scheme.

predicates.income_tax_assessment_proceeding: The matter concerns assessment of a settlor's income for income tax.
predicates.trust_income_is_distributed_to_settlor_a: The trust distributes income to the settlor as a beneficiary and also to other beneficiaries.
predicates.trust_not_revocable_within_six_years: The trust cannot be revoked within six years of its creation.

issues.definition: When a trust distributes income to the settlor and other beneficiaries and cannot be revoked within six years, the other beneficiaries' income is not attributed to the settlor until revocation becomes possible, while the settlor's own beneficial income remains taxable.

issues.legal_issue: The third proviso applies even when a settlement is deemed revocable under the first proviso.
material_facts: The Commissioner argued that the third proviso did not apply to settlements deemed revocable because of a right to retransfer income or assets or reassume control.
The Court rejected that construction and treated the first proviso as defining settlements deemed revocable for purposes of the principal clause.
issues.conclusion: The third proviso operates in respect of settlements, dispositions, or transfers that are deemed revocable by the first proviso, subject to the third proviso's conditions.
issues.legal_principle: The first proviso to s. 16(1)(c) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, deems specified settlements, dispositions, or transfers revocable for the purpose of the principal clause; the third proviso may still exclude qualifying income if its conditions are met. The Court relied on Ramji Keshavji v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay, 13 I.T.R. 105, whose explanation of the statutory scheme it approved.

predicates.income_tax_assessment_proceeding: The matter concerns an income-tax assessment involving income arising under a settlement.
predicates.settlement_is_deemed_revocable_by_retran: The settlement provides for retransfer of income or assets or gives the settlor a right to reassume control, so it is treated as revocable.
predicates.settlement_not_revocable_within_six_year: The settlement cannot in fact be revoked within six years of its creation.
predicates.settlor_gets_no_benefit_from_other_benef: The settlor derives no direct or indirect benefit from income distributed to another beneficiary.

issues.definition: The exception can protect qualifying income under a settlement treated as revocable when the settlement cannot in fact be revoked within six years and the settlor gets no benefit from the other beneficiary's income.

issues.legal_issue: A contention that a trust was actually revoked within six years will not be considered when it is raised for the first time on appeal to the Supreme Court.
material_facts: The Commissioner argued for the first time before the Supreme Court that the trust had in fact been revoked within six years.
That contention had not been raised before the revenue authorities, the Tribunal, or the High Court.
The Commissioner relied on recitals in a later deed, which the Court held did not even prima facie indicate that the trust had been revoked.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the new contention that the trust had been revoked within six years.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that it could not entertain this new ground, which had not been raised before the Revenue authorities, the Tribunal, or the High Court; it identified no earlier case as authority for this procedural ruling.

predicates.appeal_to_supreme_court: The matter is an appeal before the Supreme Court.
predicates.revocation_ground_raised_for_first_time_: A party first contends in the Supreme Court that the trust was actually revoked within the relevant period.
predicates.revocation_ground_not_raised_below: The party did not raise that contention before the lower decision-making bodies.

issues.definition: In an appeal to the Supreme Court, a contention about actual revocation is not considered when it is raised for the first time there and was not raised below.
